transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light exercise like gardening from 1 week after your surgery. Just avoid anything too strenuous or heavy lifting for about a month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for that information! I was also wondering, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question! If you were using eye gel or drops for dry eyes before your surgery, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

However, if you don't have any yet and need some, you can get preservative-free eye drops from the pharmacist. We'd recommend using them four times daily to start with.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks, that's helpful to know. I've noticed I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further. In that case, do let us know.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I appreciate the advice! One last question: should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long ago was your surgery? If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for explaining that. My surgery was about a week ago, so it sounds like it's normal. I don't have any more questions now. I appreciate your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's great to hear! So just to confirm - have all your questions about your surgery and recovery been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and best wishes with your recovery!

verdict.label: pass
verdict.reasoning: The agent successfully conveyed `normal_sensitivity_reassurance` and `mild_case_advice` in the turn starting "It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses." In the same turn, the agent also conveyed `escalation_criteria` by stating, "However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further." All three points were covered.
